subject: chemistry
title: Periodicity Adventure 3: Transition metals — coloured ions and variable OS
welcome_lead: Today you'll watch transition metals change colour and oxidation state.
meta_desc: Chemistry — transition metals, variable oxidation states, coloured ions, complex ions, catalysis.
final_note: You learned d-block metals have variable OS, form coloured ions (d-d transitions), make complex ions with ligands, and catalyse reactions.

concepts.def: Forms ions with incomplete d sub-shell

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sc to Zn share 4s and 3d orbitals close in energy → multiple OS possible.

Mn: +2, +3, +4, +6, +7 (KMnO₄ purple).
Cu: +1 (Cu₂O red), +2 (CuSO₄ blue).
Fe: +2 (pale green), +3 (yellow/brown).

Zn is not a transition metal — its only ion is Zn²⁺ [Ar]3d¹⁰ (full).

Ligands (H₂O, NH₃, Cl⁻, CN⁻) donate lone pairs → coordinate (dative) bonds.

Common shapes: octahedral (6 ligands), tetrahedral (4), square planar.

Colour: ligands split d orbitals (crystal field). Electrons absorb light to jump → complementary colour seen.

[Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ pale blue → +NH₃ → [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ deep blue.

Transition metals + their compounds catalyse:

- Fe in Haber process N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃.
- V₂O₅ in Contact process 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃.
- Ni hydrogenates margarine alkenes.
- Pt/Rh in catalytic converters (NO, CO, unburnt fuel → N₂, CO₂, H₂O).

Variable OS lets them temporarily bind/release reactants.
